To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the total disorder group of medical students who developed or died from disease had significantly more nervousness and depression, more anger under stress, more cigarette smoking, more drinking of alcoholic beverages, more insomnia, and less closeness to parents in medical school than did their healthy classmate controls.
(a) there are significant psychosocial precursors of the five disease states, and (b) there are significant differences in psychosocial precursers of the five disease groups.
the habits and family attitudes in youth of medical students who died prematurely or developed one of the five diseases were different from those who remained healthy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of precursors of disease and death.
the predictive potential of habits, family attitudes, and personality characteristics in youth.
the prediction of premature disease and premature death.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the youthful habits and family attitude patterns of the total premature death and disease group differed from those of the healthy controls to begin with; that these differences were accentuated in medical school and were significantly greater than the differences between the individual disorder groups.

the total group of 20 young medical students who later died prematurely of one of five disease entities had significantly more psychologic problems and less favorable family attitudes than the 20 healthy controls.

the young medical students who later had a disease or died prematurely were more nervous, tense, and angry under stress, and smoked more cigarettes and drank more alcohol than did their healthy classmates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the total disorder group showed significantly more nervous tension and anger under stress; more smoking and drinking; and less closeness to parents.
psychologic differences in medical students, which are present in youth, are related to the development of premature disease and to the manner of dying.
psychologic differences in the youth of medical students who subsequently develop premature disease or die of it are predictive of later disease and death.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the way we live, the habits we have, and the attitudes we hold are all predictive of our health and our longevity.
the early life habits and family attitudes that predict premature death and disease are the ones that are associated with stress.
we need to be paying much more attention to the social determinants of disease and health.
